arxiv-2012-11287.title: Topological Superconductivity in Multifold Fermion Metals
arxiv-2012-11287.creator: Jason Z. S. Gao, Xue-Jian Gao, Wen-Yu He, Xiao Yan Xu, T. K. Ng, K. T. Law
arxiv-2012-11287.description: Abstract Recently, multifold fermions characterized by band crossings with multifold degeneracy and Fermi surfaces with nontrivial Chern numbers have been discovered experimentally in AlPt Yulin and XSi(X=Rh,Co) Hassan3 ; HongDing ; Takafumi . In this work, we largely expand the family of multifold fermion materials by pointing out that several well-studied noncentrosymmetric superconductors are indeed multifold fermion metals.

arxiv-2203-15782.title: Model Selection for Maternal Hypertensive Disorders with Symmetric Hierarchical Dirichlet Processes
arxiv-2203-15782.creator: Beatrice Franzolini, Antonio Lijoi, Igor Prünster
arxiv-2203-15782.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Beatrice Franzolini, Antonio Lijoi, Igor Prünster. Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy occur in about 10% of pregnant women around the world. Though there is evidence that hypertension impacts maternal cardiac functions, the relation between hypertension and cardiac dysfunctions is only partially understood. The study of this relationship can be framed as a joint inferential problem on multiple populations, each corresponding to a different hypertensive disorder diagnosis, that combines multivariate information provided by a collection of cardiac function indexes.

arxiv-2310-17271.title: Understanding the Role of Input Token Characters in Language Models: How Does Information Loss Affect Performance?
arxiv-2310-17271.creator: Ahmed Alajrami, Katerina Margatina, Nikolaos Aletras
arxiv-2310-17271.description: Abstract Understanding how and what pre-trained language models (PLMs) learn about language is an open challenge in natural language processing. Previous work has focused on identifying whether they capture semantic and syntactic information, and how the data or the pre-training objective affects their performance.

arxiv-2311-12736.title: Spatio-Temporal Modeling of Surface Water Quality Distribution in California (1956-2023)
arxiv-2311-12736.creator: Houlin Chen, Meredith Franklin
arxiv-2311-12736.description: Abstract Surface water quality has a direct impact on public health, ecosystems, and agriculture, in addition to being an important indicator of the overall health of the environment. California’s diverse climate, extensive coastline, and varied topography lead to distinct spatial and temporal patterns in surface water.

arxiv-2404-17763.title: Likelihood-based Inference in Fully and Partially Observed Exponential Family Graphical Models with Intractable Normalizing Constants
arxiv-2404-17763.creator: Yujie Chenchen1866@purdue.edu, Anindya Bhadra bhadra@purdue.edu, Antik Chakrabortyantik015@purdue.edu
arxiv-2404-17763.description: Abstract Probabilistic graphical models that encode an underlying Markov random field are fundamental building blocks of generative modeling to learn latent representations in modern multivariate data sets with complex dependency structures. Among these, the exponential family graphical models are especially popular, given their fairly well-understood statistical properties and computational scalability to high-dimensional data based on pseudo-likelihood methods.

pmc-10644844.title: Application of 3D Printing Insole by Hemodynamics in Older Patients with Critical Limb Ischemia: Protocol for a Randomized Clinical Trial
pmc-10644844.creator: Yan Fu, Hongji Pu, Qun Huang, Peng Qiu, Deyin Zhao, Yong Cheng
pmc-10644844.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). IntroductionCritical limb ischemia (CLI) is a severe condition characterized by inadequate blood flow to the lower extremities, often leading to tissue damage and amputation. CLI is characterized by microcirculatory dysfunction, muscle tissue necrosis, and inflammation. Patients may suffer from the traumatic pain and the increase of plantar pressure, and foot care for patients with CLI has become the “last mile” to improve their life quality.

pmc-11517178.title: Results from the Swiss Cohort of Healthcare Professionals: Intention to stay and well-being
pmc-11517178.creator: I Peytremann-Bridevaux, J Jubin, C Le Saux, L Roth, E Zuercher, A Oulevey Bachmann, I Gilles
pmc-11517178.description: BackgroundIn the context of personnel shortages and high turnover rates in the healthcare sector, the Swiss COhort of Healthcare Professionals and Informal CAregivers (SCOHPICA) seeks to understand which factors act as determinants of professionals’ intent to stay in their profession and well-being, and to monitor their trajectories.

pmc-11670697.title: Sex differences in clinically diagnosed psychiatric disorders over the lifespan: a nationwide register-based study in Sweden
pmc-11670697.creator: Yihui Yang, Fang Fang, Filip K Arnberg, Ralf Kuja-Halkola, Brian M D'Onofrio, Henrik Larsson, Isabell Brikell, Zheng Chang, Ole A Andreassen, Paul Lichtenstein, Unnur A Valdimarsdóttir, Donghao Lu
pmc-11670697.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryBackgroundLimited studies exist on sex differences in incidence rates of psychiatric disorders across the lifespan. This study aims to analyze sex differences in the incidence rates of clinically diagnosed psychiatric disorders over the lifespan.MethodsWe conducted a nationwide register-based cohort study, including all individuals who were born in Sweden and lived in Sweden between 2003 and 2019, including 4,818,071 females and 4,837,829 males. We calculated sex- and age-specific standardized incidence rates for any and 10 major types of psychiatric disorders.

pmc-12413387.title: Cutting-edge technologies in neural regeneration
pmc-12413387.creator: Chang-Ping Li, Ying-Ying Wang, Ching-Wei Zhou, Chen-Yun Ding, Peng Teng, Rui Nie, Shu-Guang Yang
pmc-12413387.description: Neural regeneration stands at the forefront of neuroscience, aiming to repair and restore function to damaged neural tissues, particularly within the central nervous system (CNS), where regenerative capacity is inherently limited. However, recent breakthroughs in biotechnology, especially the revolutions in genetic engineering, materials science, multi-omics, and imaging, have promoted the development of neural regeneration.

pmc-12429373.title: Identifying Frailty Risk in Older Adults: The Predictive Value of Functional Tests and Center-of-Pressure-Based Postural Metrics
pmc-12429373.creator: Hammad S. Alhasan
pmc-12429373.description: Background/Objectives: Frailty is a multidimensional syndrome characterized by diminished physiological reserves, reduced mobility, and increased fall risk. While clinical assessments are commonly used to screen for frailty, they may not capture minor deficits in postural control. Center-of-pressure (CoP) metrics from force plates provide objective markers of postural control, yet their role in frailty screening remains underexplored.

pmc-12580443.title: Motor segmentation: a key neuromuscular impairment in people with parkinson’s disease
pmc-12580443.creator: Rebecca J. Daniels, Christopher A. Knight
pmc-12580443.description: Healthy adults (OA) achieve rapid isometric force production with a brief, high amplitude burst of neural excitation. In some people with Parkinson’s disease (PwPD), transient reductions in neural excitation (motor segmentation) reduce rates of force development (RFD) and prolong contractions.

pmc-12674269.title: Eye-tracking enables reliable pain assessment in intubated SCI patients and is not associated with self-appraisals
pmc-12674269.creator: Christina Ingwald, Robert Gaschler, Uwe Hamsen, Aileen Spieckermann, Thomas Armin Schildhauer, Oliver Cruciger, Christian Waydhas, Christopher Ull
pmc-12674269.description: AimsTo examine whether eye-tracking (ET) enables reliable self-report of pain in intubated patients with spinal cord injury (SCI) and to explore associations between pain and psychological self-appraisals.MethodsIn this prospective observational study, 75 mechanically ventilated ICU patients (46 SCI, 29 non-SCI) completed pain assessments using a Tobii Dynavox ET device.

pmc-13247828.title: High-efficiency ultra-thin CIGSe solar cells: defect engineering and back-surface field design
pmc-13247828.creator: Serap Yiğit Gezgin, M. A. Basyooni-M. Kabatas, Hamdi Şükür Kiliç
pmc-13247828.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study presents a comprehensive SCAPS-1D simulation of an ultra-thin CIGSe/CdS/i-ZnO/ITO solar cell with a 420 nm absorber layer, focusing on the influence of key physical parameters and back surface field engineering. The effects of acceptor doping density in CIGSe (Na = 1013 to 1018 cm−3), interface defect density (Ni–t = 109 to 1018 cm−3), bulk defect density (Nt = 1012 to 1020 cm−3), and electron affinity (χ = 4.35–4.65 eV) were systematically investigated.

pmc-13256000.title: Viral Sentry AI—Automated zoonotic surveillance and drug repurposing agent
pmc-13256000.creator: Cristian R Munteanu, Jose Vázquez-Naya, Eduardo Tejera
pmc-13256000.description: Zoonotic viruses capable of jumping from animal reservoirs into human populations represent a persistent and unpredictable menace to global health. To confront this challenge, we developed Viral Sentry AI, an autonomous agent designed to close the gap between viral emergence and therapeutic response.

pmc-13372052.title: NaP‐TRAP: A Versatile and Accessible Workflow to Dissect Principles of Translational Regulation and mRNA Stability
pmc-13372052.creator: Amit Gupta, Anna Z Struba, Srihari Madhavan, Ethan Strayer, Jean‐Denis Beaudoin
pmc-13372052.description: The translation of messenger RNA (mRNA) into protein is tightly regulated by both cellular trans‐factors and cis‐regulatory elements encoded within transcripts. Although transcript fate can be measured by transcript abundance or translation efficiency, separating the contribution of individual cis‐element within a single transcript is an ongoing challenge.

pmc-13455832.title: Unipolar Barrier Near‐Infrared 2D Photodetectors for 3D Image Sensors
pmc-13455832.creator: Jung Pyo Hong, Sang‐Jun Kim, Jisu Jang, Je‐Jun Lee, Seong‐Jun Han, Eungseon Yeon, Jung Woo Kim, Jongtae Ahn, Sang Yeon Kim, Hyun Woo Ko, Sunghyun Han, Seung Ah Lee, Paul Hongsuck Seo, Young‐Woo Suh, Kimoon Lee, Gunuk Wang, Dong‐Guang Zheng, Sunghee Hong, Sangin Hahn, Seon Kyu Yoon, Min‐Chul Park, Do
pmc-13455832.description: Photodetectors sensitive to the near‐infrared (NIR) range are of great importance for applications in machine vision, autonomous driving, and three‐dimensional (3D) imaging under low‐light or adverse weather conditions. Recently, two‐dimensional (2D) semiconductors have emerged as promising light‐absorbing materials for NIR detection.
